title: 3.5.18 Lab: Rewrite a Multi-Parameter Function to Take an Object
description: Take a function with three positional parameters and rewrite it to read one options object instead. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Write the positional original
steps.instructions: Write a function (the lesson calls it describeBox; name it for what you are building) that takes three positional parameters (width, height and color) and returns a string built from them.

steps.title: Rewrite it to take one object
steps.instructions: Change describeBox so it takes a single parameter, an options object, and reads width, height and color off that object with a dot.

steps.title: Call it with an options object
steps.instructions: Call describeBox with one object literal that names the three keys, and print the result. Put the object literal directly inside the call parentheses; a variable holding the object does not count.

requirements.title: function defined
requirements.description: Defines a function. Help: 3.5.16 (Objects as Named Arguments)
requirements.hint: Define the function with the function keyword and a name of your choice.

requirements.title: reads a property off the options object
requirements.description: Uses options.property in the body. Help: 3.5.16 (Objects as Named Arguments)
requirements.hint: The single parameter is the options object. Read each value off it with a dot, like options.width.

requirements.title: describeBox called with an object literal, and the result printed
requirements.description: A call to describeBox passes an object literal in braces, and what it returns is printed: the call is inside console.log, or stored in a variable that is then printed. Help: 3.5.16 (Objects as Named Arguments)
requirements.hint: Call describeBox with one object in braces naming each key, and print what it returns: console.log(describeBox({ width: 10, height: 4, color: "red" })). Pass the braces right in the call: a variable holding the object does not count.

requirements.title: result printed
requirements.description: Calls console.log. Help: 3.5.16 (Objects as Named Arguments)
requirements.hint: Print with console.log so you can see the result and check it against what you expected.

requirements.title: describeBox takes one options object and uses all three values
requirements.description: describeBox takes one options object and the text it returns is built from all three values: changing the width, the height or the color changes the text. Help: 3.5.17 (Function Taking One Options Object)
requirements.hint: describeBox should have ONE parameter, the options object. Read options.width, options.height and options.color, and build the returned string from all three.

checks.fail: A printed line says undefined or NaN: describeBox read a key the object you passed does not have. Spell each key exactly: width, height, color.

checks.expr: typeof describeBox === 'function' && describeBox.length <= 1 && (() => { const s = (o) => { const L = console.log; const cap = []; console.log = function () { cap.push(Array.prototype.map.call(arguments, String).join(' ')); }; let r; try { r = describeBox(o); } finally { console.log = L; } return r === undefined && cap.length ? cap.join('\n') : String(r); }; const r0 = s({ width: 2, height: 3, color: 'red' }); return r0 === s({ width: 2, height: 3, color: 'red' }) && s({ width: 7, height: 3, color: 'red' }) !== r0 && s({ width: 2, height: 9, color: 'red' }) !== r0 && s({ width: 2, height: 3, color: 'blue' }) !== r0; })()
checks.fail: describeBox should take one options object and build its text from all three values: describeBox({ width: 2, height: 3, color: "red" }) should change if the width, the height or the color changes.

checks.expr: typeof describeBox === 'function' && (() => { const s = (o) => { const L = console.log; const cap = []; console.log = function () { cap.push(Array.prototype.map.call(arguments, String).join(' ')); }; let r; try { r = describeBox(o); } finally { console.log = L; } return r === undefined && cap.length ? cap.join('\n') : String(r); }; try { return !s({ width: 2, height: 3, color: 'red', zzqx: 'qqzzx' }).includes('qqzzx'); } catch (e) { return false; } })()
checks.fail: describeBox should build its text from the width, height and color it reads, not hand the whole options object to something like JSON.stringify or Object.values.

checks.expr: (() => { const READS = (() => { const src = String(describeBox); const d = /^[^(]*\(\s*\{([^}]*)\}/.exec(src); if (d) return { dot: d[1].split(',').map((x) => x.trim().split(/[\s:=]/)[0]).filter((k) => /^[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*$/.test(k)), br: [], param: '' }; const m = /^(?:async\s+)?(?:function\s*[\w$]*\s*)?\(?\s*([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)/.exec(src); if (!m) return { dot: [], br: [], param: '' }; const pe = m[1].replace(/\$/g, '\\$'); const dot = []; const br = []; let x; const re = new RegExp('(?<![\\w$.])' + pe + '\\s*\\.\\s*([A-Za-z_$][\\w$]*)', 'g'); while ((x = re.exec(src))) if (!dot.includes(x[1])) dot.push(x[1]); const bd = new RegExp('(?:const|let|var)\\s*\\{([^}]*)\\}\\s*=\\s*' + pe + '(?![\\w$])').exec(src); if (bd) bd[1].split(',').map((y) => y.trim().split(/[\s:=]/)[0]).filter((k) => /^[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*$/.test(k) && !dot.includes(k)).forEach((k) => dot.push(k)); const rb = new RegExp('(?<![\\w$.])' + pe + '\\s*\\[\\s*["\x27]([^"\x27]*)["\x27]\\s*\\]', 'g'); while ((x = rb.exec(src))) if (!br.includes(x[1])) br.push(x[1]); return { dot, br, param: m[1] }; })(); return READS.dot.length >= 3; })()

requirements.title: what describeBox returns is printed, with every key filled
requirements.description: A console.log that runs prints what describeBox returned for an object literal, and no printed line says undefined (a key describeBox reads that the object does not have). A result thrown away, typed-in text, and a print that never runs do not count. Help: 3.5.16 (Objects as Named Arguments)
requirements.hint: Print the call: console.log(describeBox({ width: 10, height: 4, color: "red" })), with every key describeBox reads spelled exactly as it reads it.

checks.fail: Nothing was printed by code that runs. A console.log inside a function nobody calls, or behind a test that is never true, prints nothing.
A printed line says undefined: describeBox read a key the object you passed does not have. Check that each key is spelled exactly as describeBox reads it.
No console.log that runs prints what describeBox returned. Print the call: console.log(describeBox({ width: 10, height: 4, color: "red" })).

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote JavaScript for the lab "3.5.18 Lab: Rewrite a Multi-Parameter Function to Take an Object". The task they were given: Write a function (the lesson calls it describeBox; name it for what you are building) that takes three positional parameters (width, height and color) and returns a string built from them. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
